welcome_lead: Mean, median, mode, range and SD — summarising data the right way.

final_note: Choose your average to match your data.

concepts.def: Sum divided by count — uses every value.
Middle value when ordered — robust to outliers.
Most frequent value — only choice for nominal data.
Highest minus lowest — simple but outlier-sensitive.
Symmetrical bell curve; mean = median = mode.

walkthroughs.body_html: Mean for interval/ratio data with no extreme outliers. Median for ordinal data or skewed distributions (e.g. salaries). Mode for nominal data (most common eye colour). For income data the mean is skewed upward by high earners — median is fairer.

Range = highest - lowest; quick but sensitive to outliers. SD is more informative — square root of mean squared deviations. In a normal distribution, 68% of scores lie within ±1 SD of the mean, 95% within ±2 SD, 99.7% within ±3 SD.

Normal distribution: symmetrical, mean = median = mode. Positive skew (e.g. income): mean > median > mode; tail on the right. Negative skew: mean < median < mode; tail on the left. Skew affects which measure best summarises the data.
